issues.legal_issue: A scheme settled in a public-trust suit may reserve power to amend the scheme by application, without requiring a separate suit, when the amendment is for the administration of the trust.
material_facts: A scheme for the administration of a public religious trust was settled in a suit under Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
The scheme and the judgment settling it reserved the ability to modify the scheme as circumstances required.
The District Judge revised the scheme after an investigation into the temple’s management.
issues.conclusion: The court may amend the scheme by an application under its reserved modification clause when the change concerns administration; a separate suit under Section 92 is not required.
issues.legal_principle: Section 92(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure empowers the court to settle a scheme, and Section 92(2) does not bar an application made under a modification provision contained in that scheme. A suit to settle a scheme is analogous to an administration suit, and the decree may provide for a future change in the manner of administration without losing its finality. The court approved Chandraprasad Ramprasad v. Jinabharathi Narayanabharathi, Sri Swami Rangacharya v. Gangaram, Umeshananda Dutta Jha v. Sir Ravaneswar Prasad Singh, Manadananda Jha v. Tarakananda Jha Panda, Srijib Nyayatirtha v. Sreemant Dandy Swami Jagannath Ashram, Mahomed Waheb Hussain v. Syed Abbas Hussain, and Gangaram Govind Pashankar v. Sardar K. R. Vinchurkar; it disapproved Veeraraghavachariar v. The Advocate-General of Madras. The Privy Council schemes in Prayaga Doss Jee Varu v. Tirumala Anandam Pillai Purisa Sriranga Charylu Varu and Sevak Kirpashanker Daji v. Gopal Rao Manohar Tambekar were also referred to.

predicates.public_trust_scheme_proceeding: A proceeding is brought to settle a scheme for administering a public charitable or religious trust.
predicates.scheme_reserves_modification: The settled scheme provides that it may be modified when circumstances require.
predicates.change_concerns_administration: The proposed change concerns the administration of the trust.

issues.definition: When a proceeding settles a public-trust scheme, the scheme reserves modification, and the proposed change concerns administration, the scheme may be modified by application without a separate suit.

issues.legal_issue: The absence of interested persons from the original public-trust suit does not prevent an administrative amendment that leaves their private rights unaffected.
material_facts: The pujaris were not parties to the suit in which the temple scheme was settled.
They were interested in the trust and were bound by the scheme as members of the worshipping public in matters of administration.
The pujaris asserted that the District Judge could not revise the scheme in a way affecting them without a new suit.
The court held that their absence from the original suit did not bar an administrative amendment that did not affect their private rights.
issues.conclusion: The District Judge had jurisdiction to modify the scheme despite the pujaris not having been parties to the original suit, provided the modification concerned trust administration and did not affect their private rights.
issues.legal_principle: A suit under Section 92 of the Code of Civil Procedure is representative and binds interested persons in matters concerning the trust even if they were not parties. Their absence does not deprive the court of jurisdiction to modify the scheme for administration, but an amendment that affects their private rights cannot be justified on that basis. The court also relied on the earlier decree between the trustee and the pujaris, which recognized the hereditary character of the pujari office, the trustee’s control over the performance of duties, and the pujaris’ entitlement to hold office subject to good behaviour.

rule.if: public_trust_scheme_proceeding and interested_person_not_party and change_concerns_administration and private_rights_unchanged

predicates.public_trust_scheme_proceeding: A proceeding concerns the administration of a public charitable or religious trust under a settled scheme.
predicates.interested_person_not_party: A person interested in the trust was not a party to the suit in which the scheme was settled.
predicates.change_concerns_administration: The proposed change concerns the administration of the trust.
predicates.private_rights_unchanged: The proposed change does not affect that person's private rights.

issues.definition: A nonparty's absence does not bar an administrative scheme change when the person is interested in the trust and the change leaves that person's private rights unaffected.

issues.legal_issue: Administrative provisions in a revised temple scheme are permissible when they preserve hereditary pujaris’ private rights, with safeguards where necessary to protect those rights.
material_facts: The revised scheme regulated worship and allowed rules to require the person performing worship to know the relevant rituals, with a substitute to perform the worship if the hereditary pujari lacked that knowledge.
The court construed the substitute as one provided by the pujari, not by the managing trustee.
The revised scheme authorized the managing trustee to engage persons for other customary religious functions and set their remuneration from income other than the pujaris’ allotted offerings.

It authorized the trustee to grant leave, fine, or punish pujaris for misconduct and required prior District Judge approval for dismissal; the court added a right to appeal fines or punishment to the District Judge.

The revised scheme provided for accounting for offerings to which the pujaris were entitled under the earlier agreement, but the court required safeguards for opening the box, accounting for the money, and promptly paying the pujaris’ share after relevant expenses.
The trustee relied on statutory duties to maintain accounts, prepare a budget, and have accounts audited.
issues.conclusion: The revised scheme’s administrative provisions were within the District Judge’s jurisdiction when construed or modified to preserve the pujaris’ private rights. The court restored the revised scheme subject to its clarification and additional safeguards, including protection and prompt distribution of the pujaris’ share of offerings.
issues.legal_principle: A scheme amendment may regulate administration without trespassing on private rights. The hereditary character of an office does not exempt its holder from proper control in performing duties, but control must not interfere with private entitlements. The court applied the earlier decree recognizing the pujaris’ hereditary office subject to good behaviour and the agreement governing their share of offerings. It also considered Sections 15, 16, and 18 of the Madhya Pradesh Public Trusts Act, 1951, concerning accounts, audit, and budgets, and required accounting arrangements that served those functions while protecting the pujaris’ entitlement.

rule.if: public_trust_scheme_amendment and amendment_regulates_administration and hereditary_office_holder_has_private_entitlements and safeguards_preserve_private_entitlements

predicates.public_trust_scheme_amendment: A court is considering an amendment to a scheme for administering a public religious trust.
predicates.amendment_regulates_administration: The amendment regulates the performance of trust activities or the management and accounting of trust income.
predicates.hereditary_office_holder_has_private_ent: A hereditary office holder has private rights in the office or in a share of offerings.
predicates.safeguards_preserve_private_entitlements: The amendment is construed or supplemented with safeguards that protect those private rights.

issues.definition: An amendment regulating trust administration is valid when safeguards preserve the private entitlements of hereditary office holders.
